title: Napple Tale: Arsia in Daydream
subtitle: A mistake between worlds
summary: Napple Tale: Arsia in Daydream is Chime's platform adventure, first released for Dreamcast in Japan on 19 October 2000.
body: Napple Tale: Arsia in Daydream is Chime's platform adventure, first released for Dreamcast in Japan on 19 October 2000. Porch Arsia is taken to Napple World by mistake when the spirit guide Straynap confuses her with another target. Six Petals escape from her body into the world's separate seasons, and recovering them becomes her route home. The setting lies between ordinary life and a deeper dream, giving the journey a gentle strangeness. Yoko Kanno composed the music for an adventure that links side-view platform stages with the everyday concerns of its town.

Napple Town forms a fully three-dimensional hub where Porch meets inhabitants and helps with their problems. Routes from the town lead into stages associated with spring, summer, autumn and winter, turning seasons into places that can be visited. Porch uses a swinging weapon, double jumps and a spinning attack to move through those routes and fight enemies. Bosses wait at the end of the stages. The change between town and course gives the player a repeated rhythm: learn what somebody needs, then head into another part of the dream to continue the search.

Enemies can leave recipe pieces and other items, with recipes identifying four ingredients that combine into a Paffet. Collection therefore supports another form of making things within the world, alongside the tasks undertaken for its residents. Porch's health is represented by petals, keeping even the interface connected to the story's imagery. Straynap accompanies the journey as an imperfect guide to the dream's rules. The town's personal problems and the separate seasonal landscapes give the search a welcoming scale, allowing the adventure to move between a fantastical destination and a small favour for somebody nearby.
